name: Agentic Additive Manufacturing Alloy Evaluation (Claude Code multi-agent)

system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: a simple markdown file providing additional context and system prompts to guide tool usage
system_prompt_style.note: The harness is Claude Code with subagent markdown files. The prompt mechanism belongs to Claude Code and is not shown in this evidence. The subagent files are not in the bundle. Closest value chosen.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Tools to list existing subfolders and their contents act as guides to help the LLM navigate through potential tool input arguments
env_context_strategy.note: The paper also exposes MCP resources, but reports they proved unreliable.

context_compaction.note: Compaction is handled by the host client (Claude Code). No config surface for it is in the bundle.

observation_format.evidence_quote: the lack of fusion regimes are returned as power and velocity combinations within a list of tuples
observation_format.note: Tools also declare structured_output=True, so structured_json is possible.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: dispatch tool calls via Model Context Protocol (MCP)
tool_call_format.note: Calls go through MCP in the host client.

tool_count.note: The tool definitions live in external PyPI packages that are not in the bundle. Client built-in tools are also not enumerated.

edit_primitive.note: Editing is provided by the host client, whose tool registry is absent from the bundle.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote:
Using the
MCP Python SDK, 82 these tools can be exposed to the LLM with the appropriate decorator
function configuration as seen in Appendix A.
tool_schema_source.note: Tools exposed via MCP decorators; decorator-derived schemas likely auto_generated from type declarations but not coded without the code.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: Multi-agent workflow configuration for additive manufacturing alloy evaluation via Model Context Protocol (MCP)

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: These agents can dynamically adjust their task trajectory to the outcomes of tool call results

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: The multi-agent system is able to reason and plan through given tasks

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: utilizing Claude Sonnet 4 as the primary large language model for orchestrating tool calls
multi_agent_topology.note: The main agent delegates to three subagents: additive-manufacturing, thermo-calc and workspace.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: Claude Code utilizing subagents for Additive Manufacturing, Thermo-Calc, and Workspace

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: invoking external Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) or function calls with the user’s approval
human_in_loop.note: Approval is handled by the host MCP client.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: It primarily acts as a state management tool for storingJSONserialized class objects
short_term_state.note: State is kept as workspace JSON files.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Workspaces can be initialized via tool call (Figure 3) and are subdivided into top-level subfolders
long_term_memory.note: Workspaces persist across runs and can be listed and reused. This is a closest-value fit.

state_persistence.note: The host client's session config is not in the bundle.

self_verification.note: No run loop or config is in the bundle.

retry_policy.note: No run loop is in the bundle.

rollback.note: The host client's tool registry is absent from the bundle.

termination_condition.note: The run loop is in the host client, which is not included.

cost_controls.note: The paper lists token cost optimisation only as future work.

timeouts.note: The paper reports a hang in the property diagram tool. No timeout config is in the bundle.

execution_isolation.note: The MCP servers run locally on the host. This is inferred.

permission_model.note: The permission model belongs to the host client. The paper mentions user approval, which is covered under C5.

eval_hooks.note: The file tree is truncated. The shipped results/ are outputs, not an evaluation runner.

target_domain.evidence_quote: automate and accelerate the task of evaluating proposed additive manufacturing alloys
target_domain.note: The domain is materials science and additive manufacturing.

open_source.note: A LICENSE file exists in the tree but its contents are not shown. Thermo-Calc is proprietary.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: initial implementations show that these experiments can be performed on the latest models from OpenAI (ChatGPT) and Google (Gemini) as well
model_agnostic.note: The README supports Claude, Codex and Gemini CLI clients.
